ko_meaning: 다른 사람에게 잘못해서 마음이 편하지 않다
ko_meaning_en: To feel uneasy because you did something wrong to someone

example.en: I'm really sorry I'm late.

form.q_en: Pick the correct '-아서/어서' form of 늦다 (to be late).
form.why: The vowel in 늦 is ㅡ (not ㅏ or ㅗ), so it takes -어서: 늦어서 = because I'm late.

ko_meaning: 어른에게 미안한 마음을 말할 때 쓰는 말
ko_meaning_en: A word used to tell an older person that you are sorry

example.en: I'm sorry I couldn't do my homework.

form.q_en: Pick the correct reason form of 하다.
form.why: 하다 + -여서 becomes 해서 (because I did). -아서/어서 never takes the past tense, and -러 needs 가다/오다.

en: to be thankful; to be grateful
ko_meaning: 남이 나에게 좋은 일을 해 줘서 마음이 기쁘다
ko_meaning_en: Glad in your heart because someone did something good for you

example.en: Thank you for the present.

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 고맙다.
form.why: 고맙다 is ㅂ-irregular: the ㅂ changes to 우, so 고맙 + 어요 → 고마워요.

ko_meaning_en: To feel good because you meet someone

example.en: Nice to see you again.

form.q_en: Pick the connector that gives the reason (glad because we met).
form.why: -아서 links a reason to a feeling: 만나서 반가워요. -지만 means 'but', and -러/-려고 show purpose.

ko_meaning: 다른 사람의 좋은 일을 같이 기뻐하다
ko_meaning_en: To be happy together about someone's good news

example.en: I bought a cake to celebrate my friend's birthday.

tokens.note: a noun can describe the next noun

form.q_en: Pick the ending meaning 'in order to'.
form.why: -(으)려고 means 'in order to' and can come before any verb. -(으)러 only works before 가다/오다.

ko_meaning_en: A respectful word for father and mother

example.en: My parents live in Busan.

tokens.note: honorific -세요; the ㄹ of 살 drops

form.q_en: Pick the honorific form of 살다 for parents.
form.why: Use -(으)세요 to show respect for parents. With ㄹ-stem verbs the ㄹ drops before -세요: 살다 → 사세요.

ko_meaning_en: The man a woman is married to

example.ko: 남편은 요리를 잘하지만 청소는 안 해요.
example.roman: Nampyeoneun yorireul jalhajiman cheongsoneun an haeyo.
example.en: My husband cooks well but doesn't clean.

form.q_en: Pick the connector meaning 'but'.
form.ko: 남편은 요리를 잘하___ 청소는 안 해요.
form.why: -지만 means 'but' and links two opposite facts. -(으)려고/-(으)러 show purpose, and 하다 never takes -아서 (it becomes 해서).

ko_meaning_en: The woman a man is married to

example.en: I'm going to go to the market with my wife.

form.q_en: Pick the particle 'with' that fits after a vowel.
form.why: 와 is used after a vowel (아내), 과 after a consonant. With 같이 it means 'together with'.

ko_meaning_en: A boy born to his parents

example.en: My son can't swim yet.

form.q_en: Pick the topic particle that fits after a consonant.
form.why: 은 marks the topic after a consonant (아들); 는 is for vowels. 을 and 에 do not fit here.

ko_meaning_en: A girl born to her parents

example.en: The picture my daughter drew is pretty.

form.q_en: Pick the subject particle that fits after a consonant.
form.why: 딸 ends in a consonant, so the subject particle is 이 (가 is for vowels). Inside a modifier clause, the subject takes 이/가.

ko_meaning_en: A person who comes to a shop or a home

example.en: There aren't many customers at the store today.

form.q_en: Pick the form that makes 'not many' with -지 않다.
form.why: -지 않다 makes a negative: 많다 → 많지 않아요 (there aren't many).

ko_meaning_en: A person who lives nearby

example.en: The neighbor next door is very kind.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 친절하다 before a noun.
form.why: Adjectives take -(으)ㄴ before a noun in the present: 친절하다 → 친절한 사람. -는 is for action verbs.

ko_meaning_en: A friendly word for calling an adult man

example.en: The taxi driver knows the roads well.

tokens.note: 택시 아저씨 = a casual word for a taxi driver

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 알다 (to know).
form.why: 알 has the vowel ㅏ, so it takes -아요: 알아요. (아라요 is only how it sounds.)

ko_meaning_en: A word for calling a woman of married age

example.en: The lady at the shop gave me more rice cake.

form.q_en: Pick the honorific past form of 주다 for the lady.
form.why: Add -시- for respect, then the past -었어요: 주 + 시 + 었어요 → 주셨어요.

ko_meaning: 듣는 사람들을 모두 높여 부르는 말
ko_meaning_en: A respectful word for calling all the listeners

example.en: You can all do it too.

form.q_en: Pick the form that completes 'can do' (-(으)ㄹ 수 있다).
form.why: -(으)ㄹ 수 있다 means 'can'. 하 has no final consonant, so it takes -ㄹ: 할 수 있어요.

ko_meaning_en: The year we are in now

example.en: This year I'm going to study Korean hard.

form.q_en: Pick the form that makes a future plan.
form.why: -(으)ㄹ 거예요 talks about plans and the future. After 하 it is 할 거예요.

ko_meaning_en: The year just before this year

example.ko: 작년에 제주도에 가서 사진을 많이 찍었어요.
example.roman: Jangnyeone jejudoe gaseo sajineul mani jjigeosseoyo.
example.en: Last year I went to Jeju Island and took a lot of photos.

form.q_en: Pick the verb form for something that happened last year.
form.why: 작년 (last year) is in the past, so the last verb takes -었어요. The tense goes only on the last verb, not on 가서.

ko_meaning_en: The year right after this year

example.en: I plan to enter university next year.

form.q_en: Pick the form for a plan ('plan to').
form.why: -(으)려고 하다 means 'plan to / intend to'. -(으)러 needs 가다/오다 after it, not 하다.

ko_meaning: 어떤 것 바로 뒤에 오는 것
ko_meaning_en: The thing that comes right after something

example.en: We have to get off at the next station.

form.q_en: Pick the form meaning 'have to'.
form.why: -아야/어야 하다 means 'have to'. 내리 + 어야 shortens to 내려야: 내려야 해요.

ko_meaning_en: The week just before this week

example.en: I was busy last week, so I couldn't exercise.

tokens.note: 에 marks time, 는 the topic

form.q_en: Pick the correct reason form of 바쁘다 (to be busy).
form.why: When a stem ends in ㅡ, the ㅡ drops. The vowel before it (ㅏ in 바) picks -아서: 바빠서.

ko_meaning_en: The time from midnight until 12 noon

example.en: I'm busy in the morning because I have classes.

form.q_en: Pick the connector that gives the reason.
form.why: -어서 gives a reason: 수업이 있어서 바빠요. -지만 means 'but', and -러/-려고 show purpose.

ko_meaning_en: The time from 12 noon until the sun sets

example.ko: 오후 세 시에 친구를 만날 거예요.
example.roman: Ohu se sie chingureul mannal geoyeyo.
example.en: I'm going to meet a friend at three in the afternoon.

form.q_en: Pick the native number for 'three' before 시 (o'clock).
form.why: Hours use native numbers, and 셋 shortens to 세 before a counter: 세 시.

ko_meaning_en: The early morning before the sun rises

example.en: I got up at dawn and went to the mountain.

form.q_en: Pick the connector for 'got up and then (went)'.
form.why: -아서 links two actions in order. 나 + 아서 shortens to 나서, and the past tense goes only on the last verb.

ko_meaning: 하나를 똑같이 둘로 나눈 것 중 하나
ko_meaning_en: One of two equal parts of something

example.en: I get up at half past seven in the morning.

form.q_en: Pick the native number for 'seven' o'clock.
form.why: Hours use native numbers: 일곱 시. Minutes use Sino-Korean numbers, and 반 (half) replaces 삼십 분.

ko_meaning_en: The time from morning to night; 24 hours

example.en: I'm so busy that the day feels too short.

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 짧다 (to be short).
form.why: 짧 has the vowel ㅏ, so it takes -아요: 짧아요. The double consonant ㄹㅂ stays in writing.

ko_meaning_en: The day, shown as a month and a day

example.en: I won't forget the exam date.

form.q_en: Pick the object particle that fits after a vowel.
form.why: 날짜 ends in a vowel, so the object particle is 를 (을 is for consonants).

ko_meaning_en: A chart that shows the dates and the days of the week

example.en: Looking at the calendar, tomorrow is a holiday.

form.q_en: Pick the form meaning 'when I looked (I found that)'.
form.why: -(으)니까 can show what you found out by doing something: 보니까 = when I looked. -러 and -려고 show purpose.

ko_meaning: 지금의 차례, 또는 곧 오는 차례
ko_meaning_en: The current turn, or the one coming soon

example.en: What are you going to do this weekend?

form.q_en: Pick the word for 'this (coming)' weekend.
form.why: 이번 means 'this (current or coming)'. 지난 means 'last', which does not fit the future -(으)ㄹ 거예요; 작년 and 올해 are years.

ko_meaning_en: A day you rest from work or school

example.en: Banks don't open on holidays.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form before 않아요.
form.why: -지 않다 attaches to the verb stem: 열다 → 열지 않아요. The ㄹ stays before -지.

ko_meaning: 여름이나 겨울에 학교 수업을 쉬는 때
ko_meaning_en: A time in summer or winter when school classes stop

example.ko: 방학이 되면 할머니 집에 갈 거예요.
example.roman: Banghagi doemyeon halmeoni jibe gal geoyeyo.
example.en: When vacation starts, I'll go to my grandma's house.

form.q_en: Pick the connector meaning 'when / if'.
form.why: -(으)면 means 'when/if': 방학이 되면 = when vacation comes.

ko_meaning_en: A word for counting people

example.en: Three customers came to the restaurant.

form.q_en: Pick 'two' before the counter 명.
form.why: People are counted with native numbers, and 둘 becomes 두 before a counter: 두 명.

ko_meaning_en: A word for counting animals

example.en: I saw three rabbits at the park.

form.q_en: Pick the counter for animals.
form.why: 마리 counts animals. 명 is for people, 권 for books, and 병 for bottles.

ko_meaning_en: A word for counting books or notebooks

example.en: I borrowed three books from the library.

form.q_en: Pick 'four' before the counter 권.
form.why: Books are counted with native numbers, and 넷 shortens to 네 before a counter: 네 권.

ko_meaning: 종이나 표처럼 얇은 것을 세는 말
ko_meaning_en: A word for counting thin things like paper or tickets

example.ko: 친구하고 보려고 표를 두 장 샀어요.
example.roman: Chinguhago boryeogo pyoreul du jang sasseoyo.
example.en: I bought two tickets to watch it with my friend.

form.q_en: Pick 'one' before the counter 장.
form.why: 하나 becomes 한 before a counter: 한 장 = one sheet/ticket.

ko_meaning: 병에 든 물이나 주스를 세는 말
ko_meaning_en: A word for counting water or juice in bottles

example.ko: 편의점에서 물 한 병을 사서 마셨어요.
example.roman: Pyeonuijeomeseo mul han byeongeul saseo masyeosseoyo.
example.en: I bought a bottle of water at the convenience store and drank it.

form.q_en: Pick the connector 'bought and then (drank it)'.
form.why: -아서 links two actions where the first leads to the second. The past tense is only on 마셨어요.

ko_meaning: 컵에 든 커피나 물을 세는 말
ko_meaning_en: A word for counting coffee or water in cups

example.en: I drink two cups of coffee every morning.

form.q_en: Pick the particle meaning 'every'.
form.why: 마다 means 'every': 아침마다 = every morning.

ko_meaning_en: A word for counting age

example.en: My younger sibling is ten this year.

form.q_en: Pick 'ten' for an age with 살.
form.why: Age with 살 uses native numbers: 열 살. Sino-Korean 십 is not used with 살.

ko_meaning: 같은 일을 하는 횟수를 세는 말
ko_meaning_en: A word for counting how many times you do something

example.ko: 일주일에 두 번 수영을 하러 가요.
example.roman: Iljuire du beon suyeongeul hareo gayo.
example.en: I go swimming twice a week.

form.q_en: Pick the form for 'go to (swim)'.
form.why: -(으)러 + 가다/오다 means 'go/come to do something': 수영을 하러 가요.

ko_meaning_en: A part of a building at the same height, like the 1st or 2nd floor

example.en: Take the elevator and go up to the seventh floor.

form.q_en: Pick the number used for floor names.
form.why: Floor names use Sino-Korean numbers: 칠 층 = the 7th floor. Native 일곱 is not used for floor names.

ko_meaning: 차나 컴퓨터 같은 기계를 세는 말
ko_meaning_en: A word for counting machines like cars or computers

example.ko: 그 가게에서 자전거를 한 대 샀어요.
example.roman: Geu gageeseo jajeongeoreul han dae sasseoyo.
example.en: I bought a bicycle at that store.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for the place where you bought it.
form.ko: 그 가게___ 자전거를 한 대 샀어요.
form.why: 에서 marks the place where an action (buying) happens. 에 is for where something is or where you go.

ko_meaning_en: Going to stores and buying things

example.en: I'm going to go shopping with my older sister on the weekend.

form.q_en: Pick the correct future form of 가다.
form.why: -(으)ㄹ 거예요 is for plans. 가 has no final consonant, so it is 갈 거예요.

ko_meaning: 여러 가지 물건을 파는 아주 큰 가게
ko_meaning_en: A very big store that sells many kinds of things

example.en: The department store is expensive, so let's go to the market.

form.q_en: Pick the reason form that can come before a request.
form.why: Before a request or suggestion such as 가세요, a reason takes -(으)니까, not -아서/어서.

ko_meaning: 음식이나 생활에 필요한 물건을 파는 큰 가게
ko_meaning_en: A big store that sells food and everyday things

example.en: I went to the supermarket to buy eggs.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for the place you go to.
form.why: 에 marks the place you go to with 가다/오다.

ko_meaning_en: A small store that is open even at night

example.en: It's convenient because there's a convenience store near my house.

form.q_en: Pick the correct reason form of 있다.
form.why: 있 has the vowel ㅣ, so it takes -어서: 있어서 = because there is.

ko_meaning: 물건 값을 내다, 또는 숫자를 더하고 빼다
ko_meaning_en: To pay for things, or to add and subtract numbers

example.en: Can I pay by card?

form.q_en: Pick the particle for 'by (means of)'.
form.why: (으)로 means 'by/with (a tool or method)'. After a vowel like 카드 it is 로.

ko_meaning_en: How big or small something is

example.en: These shoes are not the right size.

form.q_en: Pick the ending that makes the long negative.
form.why: The long negative is -지 않다: 맞지 않아요 = doesn't fit. 안 해요, 없어요 and 아니에요 cannot follow -지 here.

ko_meaning_en: The money you pay to buy something

example.en: It was cheap, so I bought two.

form.q_en: Pick the correct reason form of 싸다 (to be cheap).
form.why: 싸 + 아서 shortens to 싸서 (because it's cheap). The past tense does not go on -아서.

ko_meaning: 돈 대신에 물건 값을 낼 때 쓰는 작은 것
ko_meaning_en: A small thing used instead of money to pay

example.ko: 지갑에 카드가 없어서 계산을 못 했어요.
example.roman: Jigabe kadeuga eopseoseo gyesaneul mot haesseoyo.
example.en: There was no card in my wallet, so I couldn't pay.

form.q_en: Pick the connector that gives the reason.
form.why: -어서 gives the reason: 카드가 없어서 = because there was no card. -(으)면 cannot be used with a past result.

ko_meaning: 카드가 아닌 진짜 돈, 종이돈이나 동전
ko_meaning_en: Real money, not a card: bills or coins

example.en: You have to pay cash at the market.

form.q_en: Pick the object particle that fits after a consonant.
form.why: 현금 ends in a consonant, so the object particle is 을 (를 is for vowels).

ko_meaning: 돈을 낸 것을 보여 주는 종이
ko_meaning_en: A piece of paper that shows you paid

example.en: If you don't have the receipt, you can't get a refund.

form.q_en: Pick the connector meaning 'if'.
form.why: -(으)면 means 'if': 영수증이 없으면 = if you don't have the receipt.

ko_meaning_en: To pick one out of several

example.en: I chose this bag.

form.q_en: Pick the correct past form of 고르다.
form.why: 고르다 is 르-irregular: 르 drops and an extra ㄹ is added, so 고르 + 았어요 → 골랐어요.

ko_meaning: 가지고 있던 것을 다른 것으로 하다
ko_meaning_en: To replace something you have with something else

example.ko: 셔츠를 다른 색깔로 바꿀 수 있어요?
example.roman: Syeocheureul dareun saekkallo bakkul su isseoyo?
example.en: Can I exchange the shirt for a different color?

form.q_en: Pick the particle meaning 'into / for (another one)'.
form.ko: 셔츠를 다른 색깔___ 바꿀 수 있어요?
form.why: (으)로 marks what something changes into. 색깔 ends in ㄹ, and after ㄹ you use 로, not 으로.

ko_meaning: 산 물건을 돌려주고 돈을 다시 받다
ko_meaning_en: To return something you bought and get your money back

example.en: The clothes were too small, so I got a refund.

form.q_en: Pick the correct reason form of 작다.
form.why: 작 has the vowel ㅏ, so it takes -아서: 작아서 = because they were small.

ko_meaning_en: To make the price of something cheaper

example.en: You can bargain at the market.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form before 수 있어요.
form.why: 깎 ends in a consonant, so it takes -을 수 있다: 깎을 수 있어요 = can bargain.

ko_meaning: 선물을 종이로 싸거나 음식을 가져갈 수 있게 담다
ko_meaning_en: To wrap a gift in paper, or to pack food so you can take it away

example.ko: 이 떡은 포장해서 가지고 갈 거예요.
example.roman: I tteogeun pojanghaeseo gajigo gal geoyeyo.
example.en: I'll have this rice cake packed and take it with me.

form.q_en: Pick the connector 'pack it and then (take it)'.
form.why: -아서/어서 links two steps: pack it, then take it. 하다 + -여서 → 해서, and it never takes the past tense.

ko_meaning: 여자가 허리 아래에 입는, 바지가 아닌 옷
ko_meaning_en: Clothing a woman wears below the waist that is not pants

example.en: I'm going to wear a short skirt today.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 짧다 before a noun.
form.why: Adjectives take -(으)ㄴ before a noun: 짧다 → 짧은 치마.

ko_meaning: 몸 위쪽에 입는, 단추가 있는 옷
ko_meaning_en: A top with buttons that you wear on your upper body

example.en: My shirt is dirty, so I have to do laundry.

form.q_en: Pick the correct reason form of 더럽다 (to be dirty).
form.why: 더럽다 is ㅂ-irregular: ㅂ becomes 우, so 더럽 + 어서 → 더러워서.

ko_meaning_en: Thin clothing you wear on your feet

example.en: It was cold, so I wore thick socks.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 두껍다 (thick) before a noun.
form.why: 두껍다 is ㅂ-irregular: before a noun the ㅂ becomes 우, so 두껍 + 은 → 두꺼운.

ko_meaning: 눈이 잘 보이게 눈 앞에 쓰는 물건
ko_meaning_en: Something you wear in front of your eyes to see well

example.en: I lost my glasses, so I bought new ones.

form.q_en: Pick the connector that gives the reason.
form.why: -어서 gives the reason: 잃어버려서 = because I lost them. 리 + 어서 shortens to 려서.

ko_meaning_en: What you wear on your hands when it is cold

example.en: It's cold, so wear gloves.

form.q_en: Pick the reason form that can come before a request (-세요).
form.why: Before a request like 끼세요, use -(으)니까 for the reason. 춥다 is ㅂ-irregular: 춥 + 으니까 → 추우니까.

ko_meaning_en: To put your feet into shoes or socks

example.en: We don't wear shoes inside the house.

tokens.note: 에서 marks the place of an action

form.q_en: Pick the verb used for wearing shoes.
form.why: 신다 is for shoes and socks. 입다 is for clothes, 쓰다 for hats, and 끼다 for gloves or glasses.

ko_meaning: 장갑이나 반지, 안경 같은 것을 몸에 하다
ko_meaning_en: To put on things like gloves, rings or glasses

example.en: Today I wore my glasses to school.

tokens.note: -고 = and; with wearing verbs it shows the state

form.q_en: Pick the connector meaning 'put on and (went)'.
form.why: -고 links actions: put on glasses and went. With wearing verbs, -고 also means 'wearing'.

ko_meaning_en: To remove what you are wearing

example.en: You have to take off your shoes here.

form.q_en: Pick the correct '-아야/어야' form of 벗다.
form.why: 벗 has the vowel ㅓ, so it takes -어야: 벗어야 해요 = have to take off.

en: to tie; to wear (a tie, seat belt)
ko_meaning: 끈이나 넥타이 같은 것을 풀어지지 않게 묶다
ko_meaning_en: To tie something like a string or a tie so it doesn't come loose

example.en: When you get in a car, you have to wear your seat belt.

form.q_en: Pick the connector meaning 'when / if'.
form.why: -(으)면 means 'when/if': 차에 타면 = when you get in the car.

en: to suit; to go well with
ko_meaning_en: To look good together because they match well

example.ko: 이 모자는 아빠한테 잘 어울릴 거예요.
example.roman: I mojaneun appahante jal eoullil geoyeyo.
example.en: This hat will suit Dad well.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form before 거예요.
form.why: -(으)ㄹ 거예요 makes a guess about the future: 어울릴 거예요 = will suit.

ko_meaning_en: Things like red and blue

example.en: I bought this umbrella because its color is pretty.

form.q_en: Pick the correct reason form of 예쁘다.
form.why: The ㅡ in 예쁘 drops before -어서: 예쁘 + 어서 → 예뻐서.

ko_meaning_en: The color of leaves and grass

example.en: In spring the mountains turn green.

form.q_en: Pick the particle meaning 'into (a color)'.
form.why: 초록색 ends in a consonant (not ㄹ), so it takes 으로. (으)로 shows what something changes into.

ko_meaning_en: A color like soil or coffee

example.ko: 갈색 신발은 이 바지와 어울리지 않아요.
example.roman: Galsaek sinbareun i bajiwa eoulliji anayo.
example.en: Brown shoes don't go with these pants.

form.q_en: Pick the particle 'with' that fits after a vowel.
form.ko: 갈색 신발은 이 바지___ 어울리지 않아요.
form.why: 와 is used after a vowel (바지); 과 after a consonant. 어울리다 takes 와/과 for 'go with'.

ko_meaning_en: A color made by mixing white and black

example.en: The sky is gray, so take an umbrella.

form.q_en: Pick the reason form that fits before a request (-세요).
form.why: Before a request like 가세요, a reason takes -(으)니까. -아서/어서 (including 이라서/이어서) cannot come before a request.

ko_meaning_en: Red mixed with white

example.ko: 분홍색 셔츠를 입은 사람이 제 남편이에요.
example.roman: Bunhongsaek syeocheureul ibeun sarami je nampyeonieyo.
example.en: The person wearing the pink shirt is my husband.

form.q_en: Pick the modifier form of 입다 ('who is wearing').
form.why: -(으)ㄴ after a verb makes a modifier: 셔츠를 입은 사람 = the person wearing (having put on) the shirt.

ko_meaning: 두 바퀴를 발로 돌려서 타는 것
ko_meaning_en: Something you ride by turning two wheels with your feet

example.en: I can't ride a bicycle.

form.q_en: Pick the form that means 'can't ride'.
form.why: -(으)ㄹ 수 없다 means 'cannot'. 타 has no final consonant, so it is 탈 수 없어요.

ko_meaning_en: A long vehicle that runs on rails

example.en: It's faster if you go by train.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for 'by (a means of transport)'.
form.why: (으)로 marks the means of transport. 기차 ends in a vowel, so it takes 로.

ko_meaning: 바퀴가 두 개 있고 엔진으로 가는 차
ko_meaning_en: A vehicle with two wheels that runs on an engine

example.en: Motorcycles are dangerous, so ride slowly.

form.q_en: Pick the ending for a polite request ('please ride').
form.why: -(으)세요 makes a polite request: 천천히 타세요 = please ride slowly. The other endings cannot end a sentence.

ko_meaning: 버스가 서서 사람이 타고 내리는 곳
ko_meaning_en: A place where buses stop and people get on and off

example.ko: 정류장에 사람이 많아서 버스를 못 탔어요.
example.roman: Jeongnyujange sarami manaseo beoseureul mot tasseoyo.
example.en: There were so many people at the bus stop that I couldn't get on the bus.

form.q_en: Pick the correct reason form of 많다.
form.why: 많 has the vowel ㅏ, so it takes -아서: 많아서 = because there were many.

ko_meaning_en: A place where airplanes take off and land

example.ko: 내일 아침 일찍 공항에 가야 해요.
example.roman: Naeil achim iljjik gonghange gaya haeyo.
example.en: I have to go to the airport early tomorrow morning.

form.q_en: Pick the correct '-아야' form of 가다.
form.why: 가 + 아야 shortens to 가야: 가야 해요 = have to go.

ko_meaning: 버스나 지하철에서 내려서 다른 것을 타다
ko_meaning_en: To get off a bus or subway and take another one

example.en: I'll transfer to a bus at Seoul Station.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for what you transfer to.
form.why: (으)로 marks what you change to: 버스로 갈아타다 = transfer to a bus. 버스 ends in a vowel, so 로.

ko_meaning: 어떤 일을 하는 데 시간이 들다
ko_meaning_en: For some time to be needed to do something

example.en: It takes an hour from my home to the office.

form.q_en: Pick the particle meaning 'to / as far as'.
form.why: 에서 ... 까지 means 'from ... to': 집에서 회사까지 = from home to the office.

ko_meaning_en: To set off in order to go somewhere

example.en: If we leave now, we won't be late.

form.q_en: Pick the ending that makes a guess ('won't be late, I think').
form.why: -겠- expresses a guess about what will happen: 늦지 않겠어요. The past tense does not fit after an 'if' about now.

ko_meaning_en: To reach the place you were going to

example.en: I arrived at the airport and took a taxi.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for the place you arrive at.
form.why: 도착하다 takes 에 for the place you arrive at. 에서 would mean 'from' or the place of an activity.

ko_meaning_en: To make a car move and go

example.en: I drank alcohol, so I can't drive.

form.q_en: Pick the correct reason form of 마시다.
form.why: 마시 + 어서 shortens to 마셔서 (because I drank). -아서/어서 never takes the past tense.

ko_meaning: 보통 사람들이 숟가락을 드는 손이 있는 쪽
ko_meaning_en: The side of the hand most people hold a spoon with

example.en: If you go right at the intersection, there's a post office.

form.q_en: Pick the particle that shows direction.
form.why: (으)로 shows direction. 오른쪽 ends in a consonant (not ㄹ), so it is 으로.

ko_meaning_en: The side opposite the right

example.ko: 왼쪽 다리를 다쳐서 걸을 수 없어요.
example.roman: Oenjjok darireul dachyeoseo georeul su eopseoyo.
example.en: I hurt my left leg, so I can't walk.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 걷다 before 수 없어요.
form.why: 걷다 is ㄷ-irregular: ㄷ becomes ㄹ before a vowel, so 걷 + 을 → 걸을 수 없어요.

ko_meaning_en: Straight forward without turning to the side

example.en: Cross the road and go straight.

form.q_en: Pick the connector 'cross and then (go)'.
form.why: -아서/어서 links two steps in order: cross, then go straight. It never takes the past tense.

ko_meaning_en: To go from one side of a road or river to the other

example.ko: 아이는 혼자 길을 건널 수 없어요.
example.roman: Aineun honja gireul geonneol su eopseoyo.
example.en: The child can't cross the road alone.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form before 수 없어요.
form.why: 건너 has no final consonant, so it takes -ㄹ 수 없다: 건널 수 없어요 = can't cross.

ko_meaning_en: To change direction and go another way

example.en: Turn left at the next intersection.

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite request form of 돌다.
form.why: With ㄹ-stem verbs the ㄹ drops before -세요: 돌다 → 도세요.

ko_meaning_en: A place close to somewhere

example.en: There are many good restaurants near my office.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 맛있다 before a noun.
form.why: Words ending in 있다/없다 (맛있다, 재미있다) take -는 before a noun: 맛있는 식당.

ko_meaning_en: A place where the road splits in four directions

example.en: This intersection is dangerous because there are many cars.

form.q_en: Pick the topic particle that fits after a vowel.
form.why: 는 marks the topic after a vowel (사거리); 은 is for consonants.

ko_meaning: 사람이 길을 건널 수 있게 하얀 줄을 그린 곳
ko_meaning_en: A place with white lines painted so people can cross the road

example.en: You have to cross carefully at crosswalks.

tokens.note: -아서/어서 can show the way you do something

form.q_en: Pick the particle for the place where you do something.
form.why: 에서 marks the place where you do something (cross carefully), and 는 adds 'as for'.

ko_meaning: 빨간불, 초록불로 가고 서는 것을 알려 주는 등
ko_meaning_en: A light that tells you to go or stop with red and green

example.en: Cross when the traffic light turns green.

form.q_en: Pick the connector meaning 'when / if'.
form.why: -(으)면 means 'when/if': 바뀌면 건너세요 = cross when it changes.

ko_meaning_en: A structure built for people to live or work in

example.en: That tall building is our company.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 높다 before a noun.
form.why: Adjectives take -(으)ㄴ before a noun: 높다 → 높은 건물.

ko_meaning_en: A place where you send letters or packages

example.en: I went to the post office to send a letter home.

form.q_en: Pick the purpose form before 가다 ('to send').
form.why: -(으)러 + 가다 means 'go to do': 보내러 갔어요 = went to send.

ko_meaning_en: A place that sells medicine

example.en: I have a headache, so I'm going to go to the pharmacy.

form.q_en: Pick the correct reason form of 아프다.
form.why: The ㅡ of 아프 drops, and the vowel before it (ㅏ) picks -아서: 아파서.

ko_meaning_en: A shop that sells books

example.ko: 서점에서 한국어 책을 사고 커피를 마셨어요.
example.roman: Seojeomeseo hangugeo chaegeul sago keopireul masyeosseoyo.
example.en: I bought a Korean book at the bookstore and had coffee.

form.q_en: Pick the connector meaning 'and (then)'.
form.why: -고 lists actions one after another: 책을 사고 커피를 마셨어요.

ko_meaning_en: A shop where you drink coffee or tea

example.en: I want to read a book at a quiet cafe.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for where an action happens.
form.why: 에서 marks the place where an action (reading) happens. 에 is for where something is or where you go.

ko_meaning: 머리를 자르거나 예쁘게 해 주는 곳
ko_meaning_en: A place where they cut or style your hair

example.en: I'm going to go to the hair salon to get a haircut.

form.q_en: Pick the correct past form of 자르다 (to cut).
form.why: 자르다 is 르-irregular: 자르 + 았어요 → 잘랐어요. (자랐어요 comes from 자라다, 'to grow'.)

ko_meaning_en: A place where you watch movies or plays

example.ko: 극장이 너무 멀어서 집에서 영화를 봤어요.
example.roman: Geukjangi neomu meoreoseo jibeseo yeonghwareul bwasseoyo.
example.en: The theater was too far, so I watched a movie at home.

form.q_en: Pick the correct reason form of 멀다 (to be far).
form.why: 멀 has the vowel ㅓ, so it takes -어서: 멀어서. The ㄹ stays before 어.

ko_meaning: 옛날 물건이나 귀한 물건을 모아 보여 주는 곳
ko_meaning_en: A place that collects and shows old or valuable objects

example.en: You must not take photos in the museum.

form.q_en: Pick the form meaning 'if you take (photos)'.
form.why: 찍 ends in a consonant, so it takes -으면: 찍으면 안 돼요 = you must not take (photos).

ko_meaning_en: A place where police officers work

example.en: If you go to the police station, they will help you.

form.q_en: Pick the correct future form of 도와주다 (to help).
form.why: -(으)ㄹ 거예요 makes a future guess: 도와줄 거예요 = (they) will help.

ko_meaning: 여행하는 사람이 돈을 내고 자는 큰 건물
ko_meaning_en: A big building where travelers pay to sleep

example.en: This hotel is clean, but it's too expensive.

form.q_en: Pick the connector meaning 'but'.
form.why: -지만 means 'but' and links two contrasting facts. -(으)러/-(으)려고 express purpose, and 깨끗한 must come before a noun.

ko_meaning: 다른 나라에서 자기 나라의 일을 하는 곳
ko_meaning_en: An office in another country that does work for its own country

example.en: I have to go to the embassy to get a visa.

form.q_en: Pick the form meaning 'have to (go)'.
form.why: -아야/어야 하다 means 'have to': 가 + 아야 → 가야 해요.

ko_meaning: 밥과 같이 먹는 여러 가지 음식
ko_meaning_en: The various foods you eat together with rice

example.en: This restaurant has lots of side dishes, so I like it.

tokens.note: 은 marks the topic after a consonant
이 marks the subject after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the ending that means 'so' after 많다.
form.why: The stem 많 has ㅏ, so it takes -아서: 많아서. -어서 is for other vowels.

ko_meaning: 고기나 채소를 넣고 끓인, 국보다 물이 적은 음식
ko_meaning_en: A dish of meat or vegetables boiled with less water than soup

example.en: The kimchi stew my grandma made is the most delicious.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel
past noun modifier: 끓이 + ㄴ → 끓인

form.q_en: Pick the modifier for 'that grandma made'.
form.why: After a vowel stem the past modifier is just -ㄴ: 끓이 + ㄴ → 끓인. 끓은 would come from 끓다 'to boil (by itself)'.

ko_meaning: 고기를 달고 짜게 만들어서 구운 한국 음식
ko_meaning_en: A Korean dish of meat made sweet and salty and then grilled

example.en: Bulgogi is sweet, so even children eat it well.

tokens.note: 는 marks the topic after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 달다 + -아서/어서 ('sweet, so').
form.why: 달 has ㅏ, so it takes -아서: 달아서. ㄹ only drops before ㄴ, ㅂ or ㅅ, not here.

ko_meaning: 밥에 여러 가지 채소와 고추장을 넣고 섞어 먹는 음식
ko_meaning_en: Rice eaten mixed with various vegetables and red pepper paste

example.en: Bibimbap is spicy but delicious.

tokens.note: 은 marks the topic after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the topic particle for 비빔밥.
form.why: 비빔밥 ends in a consonant (ㅂ), so the topic particle is 은. 는 follows a vowel, and 을/에 do not fit.

ko_meaning_en: A Korean food made from rice

example.en: I bought rice cakes at the market and ate them.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens
을 marks the object after a consonant
-아서 links two actions: 사 + 아서 → 사서

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 사다 + -아서 ('bought and then').
form.why: 사 + 아서 → 사서 (the two ㅏ merge). -아서 never takes the past tense, so 샀어서 is wrong.

ko_meaning: 고추처럼 입 안이 뜨겁고 아픈 맛이 나다
ko_meaning_en: To have a hot, stinging taste like chili pepper

example.en: The kimchi was spicy, so I drank water.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 맵다 + -아서/어서.
form.why: 맵다 is ㅂ-irregular: ㅂ becomes 우 before a vowel, so 맵 + 어서 → 매워서.

ko_meaning_en: To taste strongly of salt

example.ko: 찌개가 너무 짜서 물을 더 넣었어요.
example.roman: Jjigaega neomu jjaseo mureul deo neoeosseoyo.
example.en: The stew was too salty, so I added more water.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 짜다 + -아서 ('salty, so').
form.why: 짜 + 아서 → 짜서 (the two ㅏ merge). -아서 never takes the past tense, so 짰어서 is wrong.

ko_meaning_en: To taste like sugar

example.en: I don't like sweet food.

tokens.note: 달 + ㄴ → 단 (ㄹ drops before ㄴ)

form.q_en: Pick the noun-modifier form of 달다 ('sweet food').
form.why: For a ㄹ-stem adjective, ㄹ drops and -ㄴ is added: 달 + ㄴ → 단.

ko_meaning_en: To taste like a lemon

example.en: If the juice is sour, add some sugar.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 시다 + -(으)면 ('if it is sour').
form.why: After a vowel stem, just add -면: 시 + 면 → 시면. -으면 is only for consonant stems.

ko_meaning_en: Food has little salt, so the taste is weak

example.en: Hospital food is bland, but it is good for your health.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 싱겁다 + -지만 ('bland, but').
form.why: -지만 attaches straight to the stem: 싱겁 + 지만. The ㅂ only changes before a vowel (싱거워요).

ko_meaning_en: White powder that makes food salty

example.en: I need to add a little more salt.

tokens.note: 을 marks the object after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the correct 'have to' form of 넣다.
form.why: 넣 has ㅓ (not ㅏ or ㅗ), so it takes -어야: 넣어야 해요 = have to put in.

ko_meaning_en: White powder that gives a sweet taste

example.en: I don't put sugar in my coffee.

tokens.note: 을 marks the object after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the correct ending for 'do not'.
form.why: -지 않다 means 'not'. 않다 is spelled with ㄶ and takes -아요: 않아요.

ko_meaning_en: The white grain before it is cooked into rice

example.en: I'm going to go to the supermarket to buy rice.

tokens.note: 을 marks the object after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the form that means 'to buy' (purpose of going).
form.why: -(으)러 shows the purpose of going. After a vowel stem add -러: 사 + 러 → 사러.

ko_meaning_en: A round vegetable that grows in the ground

example.en: Put in the potatoes and meat, then boil it.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 넣다 + -고 ('put in and then').
form.why: -고 goes straight on the stem with no extra vowel: 넣 + 고 → 넣고 (said [너코]).

ko_meaning_en: A round vegetable that makes you cry when you cut it

example.en: When I cut onions, tears come out.

tokens.note: 를 marks the object after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 자르다 + -(으)면.
form.why: 자르 ends in a vowel, so just add -면: 자르면. The 르 change (잘라) only happens before -아/어.

ko_meaning_en: Tea made from green leaves

example.en: Green tea is good for the body, so I drink it every day.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct present form of 마시다.
form.why: 마시 + 어요 → 마셔요 (ㅣ + ㅓ join into ㅕ).

ko_meaning_en: An alcoholic drink with foam, made from barley

example.en: On hot days, a cold beer is great.

tokens.note: ㅂ irregular modifier: 덥 + 은 → 더운
에 marks time, 는 makes it the topic
가 marks the subject after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the subject particle for 맥주.
form.why: 맥주 ends in a vowel, so the subject particle is 가. 이 follows a consonant.

ko_meaning: 맥주, 소주, 와인 같은 마실 것
ko_meaning_en: Drinks such as beer, soju and wine

example.en: I have to drive, so I can't drink.

tokens.note: 을 marks the object after a consonant
못 + verb = cannot; said [몬] before ㅁ

form.q_en: Pick the word that means 'cannot'.
form.why: 못 before a verb means 'cannot'. 없, 아니 and 말 cannot negate a verb this way.

ko_meaning: 작고 빨간, 봄에 먹는 단 과일
ko_meaning_en: A small, red, sweet fruit eaten in spring

example.en: If strawberries are cheap, I'll buy a lot.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct future form of 사다.
form.why: After a vowel stem, -(으)ㄹ 거예요 adds just ㄹ: 사 + ㄹ → 살 거예요.

ko_meaning: 길고 노란 껍질이 있는 단 과일
ko_meaning_en: A sweet fruit with a long yellow peel

example.en: I ate two bananas in the morning.

tokens.note: 둘 becomes 두 before a counter

form.q_en: Pick the right number before the counter 개.
form.why: Counters like 개 use native numbers, and 둘 becomes 두 before a counter. Sino-Korean 이 is not used with 개.

ko_meaning_en: To cook meat or bread over a fire or in heat

example.en: Yesterday I grilled meat with my family and we ate it.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 굽다 + -어서.
form.why: 굽다 is ㅂ-irregular: ㅂ becomes 우 before a vowel, so 굽 + 어서 → 구워서.

ko_meaning: 물이나 음식을 아주 뜨겁게 해서 거품이 나게 하다
ko_meaning_en: To heat water or food until it bubbles

example.en: I boiled some water and had coffee.

tokens.note: 를 marks the object after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 끓이다 + -어서.
form.why: 끓이 + 어서 → 끓여서. 끓다 means 'to boil' by itself and cannot take 물을, and -어서 never takes the past tense.

ko_meaning_en: To cook food in oil while stirring it

example.en: Onions get sweet when you stir-fry them.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 볶다 + -(으)면.
form.why: 볶 ends in a consonant, so it takes -으면: 볶으면.

ko_meaning_en: To divide something with a knife or scissors

example.en: I got my hair cut at the hair salon.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the correct past form of 자르다.
form.why: 자르다 is 르-irregular: 자르 + 았어요 → 잘랐어요. 자랐어요 comes from 자라다 'to grow'.

ko_meaning_en: To make something go inside

example.ko: 오늘 비가 오니까 가방에 우산을 넣으세요.
example.roman: Oneul biga onikka gabang-e usaneul neoeuseyo.
example.en: It's raining today, so put an umbrella in your bag.

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite request form of 넣다.
form.why: 넣 ends in a consonant, so it takes -으세요: 넣으세요.

ko_meaning: 식당에서 파는 음식의 이름과 값을 쓴 것
ko_meaning_en: A list of the names and prices of the food a restaurant sells

example.ko: 메뉴에 없는 음식은 시킬 수 없어요.
example.roman: Menyue eomneun eumsigeun sikil su eopseoyo.
example.en: You can't order food that isn't on the menu.

form.q_en: Pick the modifier form of 없다 ('that isn't there').
form.why: 있다 and 없다 take -는 when they describe a noun in the present: 없는 음식.

ko_meaning: 식당이나 가게에서 음식이나 물건을 달라고 하다
ko_meaning_en: To ask for food or goods at a restaurant or shop

example.en: I ordered the food and waited an hour.

tokens.note: 하나 becomes 한 before a counter

form.q_en: Pick the form that means 'ordered and then'.
form.why: -고 links two actions in order and goes straight on the stem: 주문하고. -(으)러 needs 가다/오다 after it.

en: to order (food); to make someone do
ko_meaning: 음식을 가져다 달라고 하다; 다른 사람에게 일을 하게 하다
ko_meaning_en: To ask for food to be brought; to make someone else do a job

example.en: We ordered pizza and ate it at home.

tokens.note: 를 marks the object after a vowel
에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 시키다 + -어서.
form.why: 시키 + 어서 → 시켜서 (ㅣ + ㅓ → ㅕ). -어서 never takes the past tense.

ko_meaning_en: To have eaten a lot so your stomach is full

example.en: I'm so full that I can't eat any more.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 배부르다 + -어서.
form.why: 배부르다 is 르-irregular: 르 + 어 becomes ㄹ러, so 배부르 + 어서 → 배불러서.

ko_meaning_en: To want to drink water

example.en: I exercised, so I'm thirsty.

form.q_en: Pick the correct present form of 목마르다.
form.why: 목마르다 is 르-irregular. 마 has ㅏ, so 마르 + 아요 → 말라요: 목말라요.

ko_meaning_en: The place at home where you make food

example.en: My older brother is making ramen in the kitchen.

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject after a consonant
에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the particle for the place where an action happens.
form.why: 에서 marks the place where an action (cooking) happens. 에 is for where something is or where you go.

ko_meaning_en: The place where you wash your hands or use the toilet

example.en: The bathroom was dirty, so I cleaned it.

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 더럽다 + -어서.
form.why: 더럽다 is ㅂ-irregular: ㅂ becomes 우 before a vowel, so 더럽 + 어서 → 더러워서.

ko_meaning: 가족이 같이 앉아서 쉬는 넓은 방
ko_meaning_en: The large room where the family sits and relaxes together

example.en: The living room is spacious and bright.

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the correct spelling of 밝다 in the present.
form.why: 밝 has ㅏ, so it takes -아요: 밝아요. It sounds like [발가요] but is spelled 밝아요.

ko_meaning_en: A big machine that keeps food cold

example.en: There's beer in the fridge, so help yourself.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for where something is (with 있다).
form.why: With 있다, use 에 for the place where something is. 에서 is for where an action happens.

ko_meaning_en: A machine that washes clothes

example.en: Laundry is easy because there's a washing machine.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 있다 + -(으)니까.
form.why: 있 ends in a consonant, so it takes -으니까: 있으니까.

ko_meaning: 여러 사람이 앉을 수 있는 크고 편한 의자
ko_meaning_en: A big, comfortable seat that several people can sit on

example.en: I sat on the sofa and read a book.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 앉다 + -아서.
form.why: 앉 has ㅏ, so it takes -아서: 앉아서 (said [안자서]).

ko_meaning_en: A machine you can watch broadcasts on

example.ko: 텔레비전을 너무 많이 보면 눈이 아파요.
example.roman: Tellebijeoneul neomu mani bomyeon nuni apayo.
example.en: If you watch too much TV, your eyes hurt.

tokens.note: 을 marks the object after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 보다 + -(으)면.
form.why: 보 ends in a vowel, so just add -면: 보면.

ko_meaning_en: An object you look into to see your face or body

example.en: I looked in the mirror and put on my hat.

tokens.note: 을 marks the object after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the verb used for putting on a hat.
form.why: Hats take 쓰다. 입다 is for clothes, 신다 for shoes and socks, and 매다 for ties.

ko_meaning_en: A large piece of furniture where you keep clothes

example.en: I put the winter clothes in the wardrobe.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for where you put something.
form.why: 넣다 takes 에 for the place things go into. 에서 marks where an action happens.

ko_meaning: 잘 때 몸 위에 덮는 크고 두꺼운 천
ko_meaning_en: A big, thick cloth you cover yourself with when you sleep

example.ko: 날씨가 추워서 이불을 하나 더 샀어요.
example.roman: Nalssiga chuwoseo ibureul hana deo sasseoyo.
example.en: It got cold, so I bought one more blanket.

tokens.note: 을 marks the object after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the word for 'one' with no counter after it.
form.why: Without a counter, 'one' is 하나. 한 is used only right before a counter (한 개).

ko_meaning_en: To make a dirty place clean

example.en: Guests are coming, so I have to clean the room.

form.q_en: Pick the form that means 'have to clean'.
form.why: -아야/어야 하다 means 'have to': 청소하 + 여야 → 청소해야 해요.

ko_meaning_en: To wash dirty clothes clean with water

example.en: If the weather is nice, I'll do the laundry.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 좋다 + -(으)면.
form.why: 좋 ends in a consonant, so it takes -으면: 좋으면 (said [조으면]).

ko_meaning_en: To make a light or a machine start working

example.en: It's dark, so turn on the light.

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite request form of 켜다.
form.why: 켜 ends in a vowel, so just add -세요: 켜세요.

ko_meaning_en: To make a light or a machine stop working

example.en: I turned off the TV and went to sleep.

form.q_en: Pick the past tense of 끄다.
form.why: The ㅡ of 끄 drops before -어: 끄 + 었어요 → 껐어요.

ko_meaning: 닫혀 있는 문이나 창문을 움직여서 안이 보이게 하다
ko_meaning_en: To move a closed door or window so the inside is open

example.en: It was hot, so I opened the window.

form.q_en: Pick the form of 열다 before 수 있어요 ('can open').
form.why: A ㄹ-stem just keeps its ㄹ: 열 + ㄹ 수 있다 → 열 수 있다 (not 열을).

ko_meaning_en: To shut something that is open

example.en: The wind was blowing, so I closed the window.

form.q_en: Pick the correct past form of 닫다.
form.why: 닫다 is regular (not like 듣다 → 들어요), and 닫 has ㅏ: 닫 + 았어요 → 닫았어요.

ko_meaning_en: To go from outside to inside

example.en: My younger sibling got angry and went into their room.

form.q_en: Pick the correct past form of 들어가다.
form.why: 가 + 았어요 → 갔어요 (the two ㅏ merge), so 들어가다 → 들어갔어요.

ko_meaning_en: To go from inside to outside

example.ko: 비가 와서 밖에 나갈 수 없어요.
example.roman: Biga waseo bakke nagal su eopseoyo.
example.en: It's raining, so I can't go outside.

form.q_en: Pick the form of 나가다 before 수 없어요 ('can't go out').
form.why: -(으)ㄹ 수 없다: after a vowel stem add ㄹ, so 나가 + ㄹ → 나갈 수 없어요.

ko_meaning_en: To come from outside to inside

example.en: It's cold outside, so come in quickly.

form.q_en: Pick the 'because' form that can come before a request.
form.why: Before a request like -(으)세요, use -(으)니까 for 'because'. -아서/어서 cannot come before a request.

ko_meaning_en: To come from inside to outside

example.en: The movie ended and I came out of the theater.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for 'out of (a place)'.
form.why: With 나오다, 에서 marks the place you come out of. 에 would mark the place you come to.

ko_meaning: 좋아해서 시간이 있을 때 자주 하는 일
ko_meaning_en: Something you like and often do when you have time

example.en: I want to meet friends who have the same hobby.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the modifier form of 같다 ('the same').
form.why: 같다 is an adjective, so the present modifier is -은: 같 + 은 → 같은. -는 is for verbs.

ko_meaning_en: Going up a mountain

example.en: I bought new shoes to go hiking.

form.q_en: Pick the form that means 'in order to go'.
form.why: -(으)려고 means 'in order to' and works with any main verb. -(으)러 only works when the main verb is 가다/오다.

ko_meaning: 물에서 팔과 다리를 움직여 앞으로 가는 운동
ko_meaning_en: Exercise of moving through water with your arms and legs

example.en: I want to learn to swim, but I don't have time.

tokens.note: 을 marks the object after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the connector meaning 'but'.
form.why: -지만 shows contrast ('but'). -어서 and -(으)니까 mean 'because', and -(으)면 means 'if'.

ko_meaning_en: Catching fish

example.en: I went fishing with my dad on the weekend.

form.q_en: Pick the ending that shows the purpose of going.
form.why: -(으)러 + 가다 means 'go in order to do': 낚시하러 갔어요 = went fishing.

ko_meaning_en: Something fun you play on a computer or phone

example.ko: 동생은 게임을 하면 밥도 안 먹어요.
example.roman: Dongsaeng-eun geimeul hamyeon bapdo an meogeoyo.
example.en: When my younger brother plays games, he doesn't even eat.

tokens.note: 을 marks the object after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the particle that means 'even'.
form.ko: 동생은 게임을 하면 밥___ 안 먹어요.
form.why: 도 means 'also / even': 밥도 안 먹어요 = doesn't even eat. 먹다 needs an object, so 밥이 is wrong.

ko_meaning: 발로 공을 차서 골에 넣는 운동
ko_meaning_en: A sport where you kick a ball into a goal

example.en: My son is good at soccer, so he's famous at school.

tokens.note: 를 marks the object after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 잘하다 + -아서/어서.
form.why: 하다 verbs become 해서: 잘하 + 여서 → 잘해서. -아서/어서 never takes the past tense.

ko_meaning_en: A sport where you hit a ball with a bat and run

example.en: I'm going to watch baseball this evening.

tokens.note: 를 marks the object after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct future form of 보다.
form.why: After a vowel stem, add ㄹ: 보 + ㄹ → 볼 거예요 = will watch.

ko_meaning: 공을 손으로 던져서 높은 바구니에 넣는 운동
ko_meaning_en: A sport where you throw a ball by hand into a high basket

example.en: He's tall, so he's good at basketball.

tokens.note: 를 marks the object after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 크다 + -어서.
form.why: The ㅡ of 크 drops before -어: 크 + 어서 → 커서. -어서 never takes the past tense.

ko_meaning: 그물을 사이에 두고 라켓으로 공을 치는 운동
ko_meaning_en: A sport where you hit a ball over a net with a racket

example.en: My older sister plays tennis every morning.

tokens.note: 를 marks the object after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the verb Koreans use with 테니스.
form.why: You 'hit' tennis: 테니스를 치다 → 쳐요. 타다 is for rides, 부르다 for songs and 신다 for shoes.

ko_meaning_en: A Korean martial art that uses the hands and feet

example.en: My daughter is planning to learn taekwondo.

tokens.note: 를 marks the object after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the ending for 'plan to' (-(으)려고 하다).
form.why: 배우 ends in a vowel, so add -려고: 배우려고 해요 = plans to learn. -으려고 is for consonant stems.

ko_meaning_en: To make a picture with a pencil or brush

example.en: The child drew Mom's face.

tokens.note: a noun before a noun can mean 'of'

form.q_en: Pick the correct past form of 그리다.
form.why: 그리 + 었어요 → 그렸어요 (ㅣ + ㅓ join into ㅕ).

ko_meaning_en: To move your body to music

example.en: I danced with my friends at the party.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the correct past form of 춤추다.
form.why: 추 + 었어요 → 췄어요 (ㅜ + ㅓ join into ㅝ).

ko_meaning: 손이나 물건으로 세게 때리다; 피아노나 테니스 같은 것을 하다
ko_meaning_en: To strike hard; to play the piano, tennis and so on

example.en: If I play the guitar in the evening, my neighbors don't like it.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 치다 + -(으)면.
form.why: 치 ends in a vowel, so just add -면: 치면.

ko_meaning_en: To walk slowly while relaxing

example.en: After dinner, I took a walk in the park.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 먹다 + -고 ('ate and then').
form.why: -고 goes straight on the stem: 먹 + 고 → 먹고.

ko_meaning: 재미있는 것이나 새로운 곳을 보며 다니다
ko_meaning_en: To go around looking at interesting things or new places

example.en: When I go to Seoul, I want to look around the museums.

form.q_en: Pick the form that goes with 싶어요 ('want to').
form.why: 'Want to' is -고 싶다: 구경하고 싶어요. The other endings cannot go before 싶다.

ko_meaning_en: To have nothing to do, so nothing is fun

example.en: I had nothing to do on the weekend, so I was bored.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 없다 + -어서.
form.why: 없 has ㅓ, so it takes -어서: 없어서 (said [업써서]).

en: to be scary; to be afraid
ko_meaning: 어떤 것 때문에 마음이 놀라고 불안하다
ko_meaning_en: To feel startled and uneasy because of something

example.en: Walking alone at night is scary.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 걷다 + -(으)면.
form.why: 걷다 is ㄷ-irregular: ㄷ becomes ㄹ before a vowel, so 걷 + 으면 → 걸으면. 걸면 comes from 걸다 'to hang'.

ko_meaning_en: To feel sad because no one is with you

example.en: I live alone abroad, so I'm lonely.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 살다 + -아서 ('live, so').
form.why: 살 has ㅏ, so it takes -아서: 살아서. ㄹ stays because the ending starts with a vowel.

ko_meaning: 나쁜 일이 생길 것 같아서 마음이 편하지 않다
ko_meaning_en: To feel uneasy because something bad might happen

example.en: My mom will worry, so I have to go home early.

form.q_en: Pick the form that means 'have to go in (home)'.
form.why: -아야/어야 하다 means 'have to': 들어가 + 아야 → 들어가야 해요.

en: to be enjoyable; to be fun
ko_meaning_en: To feel good and have fun

example.en: Have a nice weekend!

tokens.note: ㅂ irregular modifier: 즐겁 + 은 → 즐거운

form.q_en: Pick the modifier form of 즐겁다.
form.why: 즐겁다 is ㅂ-irregular: ㅂ becomes 우 before -은, so 즐겁 + 은 → 즐거운.

en: to be surprised; to be startled
ko_meaning: 생각하지 못한 일 때문에 갑자기 마음이 크게 움직이다
ko_meaning_en: To be suddenly shaken by something you didn't expect

example.en: A cat suddenly came out, and I was startled.

form.q_en: Pick the correct past form of 놀라다.
form.why: 놀라 + 았어요 → 놀랐어요. 놀랬어요 is a common spelling mistake.

ko_meaning_en: To shed tears because you are sad or hurt

example.en: The baby is crying because it's hungry.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 배고프다 + -아서/어서.
form.why: The ㅡ of 프 drops, and the vowel before it (고) has ㅗ, so it takes -아서: 배고파서.

ko_meaning: 기쁘거나 재미있어서 얼굴이 밝아지거나 소리를 내다
ko_meaning_en: To brighten your face or make a sound because you are happy or amused

example.en: I heard my friend's story and laughed a lot.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 듣다 + -고.
form.why: 듣다 keeps ㄷ before a consonant: 듣고. It changes to ㄹ only before a vowel (들어요). 들고 comes from 들다 'to hold'.

ko_meaning: 어떤 사람이나 것을 아주 좋아하고 아끼다
ko_meaning_en: To like and care about someone or something very much

example.en: Dad really loves Mom.

tokens.note: 를 marks the object after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the particle for the person who is loved.
form.why: 사랑하다 takes an object, so 엄마 needs 를 (after a vowel). 가 marks a subject, and 은 follows a consonant.

ko_meaning_en: To not like

example.en: Cats hate water.

form.q_en: Pick the form that fits after 물을 (an object).
form.why: 싫어하다 is a verb and takes an object with 을/를. 싫다 is an adjective and needs 이/가 (물이 싫어요).

ko_meaning_en: The whole of a person or animal, from head to foot

example.ko: 몸이 안 좋아서 회사에 못 갔어요.
example.roman: Momi an joaseo hoesae mot gasseoyo.
example.en: I wasn't feeling well, so I couldn't go to work.

tokens.note: 몸이 안 좋다 = to feel unwell

form.q_en: Pick the connector meaning 'so, because'.
form.why: -아서 gives the reason: 안 좋아서 = because I wasn't well. -(으)면 means 'if', and 좋을 cannot link two clauses.

ko_meaning_en: The part between the head and the body

example.en: I caught a cold, so my throat hurts.

tokens.note: 감기에 걸리다 = to catch a cold
이 marks the subject after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the correct present form of 아프다.
form.why: The ㅡ of 프 drops, and 아 has ㅏ, so it takes -아요: 아파요.

ko_meaning: 목 아래 양쪽 옆에 있는 부분
ko_meaning_en: The part on each side below the neck

example.en: My older brother is tall and has broad shoulders.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 크다 + -고 ('tall and').
form.why: -고 goes straight on the stem with no change: 크 + 고 → 크고.

ko_meaning_en: The middle part of the body, behind the stomach

example.en: My lower back hurts, so I'm going to go to the hospital.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the form for 'plan to go' (-(으)려고 하다).
form.why: -(으)려고 하다 means 'plan to': 가려고 해요. -(으)러 needs 가다/오다 right after it, not 하다.

ko_meaning_en: The part in the middle of the leg that bends

example.en: I fell down and hurt my knee.

tokens.note: 을 marks the object after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the object particle for 무릎.
form.why: 무릎 ends in a consonant (ㅍ), so the object particle is 을. 를 follows a vowel.

ko_meaning: 목이 아플 때 '콜록' 하고 나오는 소리
ko_meaning_en: The 'cough cough' sound that comes out when your throat hurts

example.en: I kept coughing, so I took some medicine.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 나다 + -아서.
form.why: 나 + 아서 → 나서 (the two ㅏ merge). -아서 never takes the past tense.

ko_meaning: 감기에 걸렸을 때 코에서 나오는 물
ko_meaning_en: Liquid that comes out of your nose when you have a cold

example.en: If you have a runny nose, take this medicine.

tokens.note: 콧물이 나다 = to have a runny nose
드시다 = polite word for 먹다; -(으)세요 = request

form.q_en: Pick the connector meaning 'if'.
form.why: -(으)면 means 'if'. -아서 cannot come before a request like -(으)세요, and -지만 means 'but'.

ko_meaning_en: Pain in the head

example.en: If you have a headache, you should rest.

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the correct 'have to' form of 쉬다.
form.why: 쉬 has ㅟ (not ㅏ or ㅗ), so it takes -어야: 쉬어야 해요.

ko_meaning_en: To get injured somewhere on your body

example.en: The hand I hurt yesterday still hurts.

tokens.note: past noun modifier: 다치 + ㄴ → 다친

form.q_en: Pick the modifier for 'that I hurt yesterday' (past).
form.why: For a past action, a verb takes -(으)ㄴ before a noun: 다치 + ㄴ → 다친. -는 is present, -(으)ㄹ is future.

ko_meaning_en: For a sick body to become healthy again

example.en: If you take the medicine, you'll get better soon.

form.q_en: Pick the correct future form of 낫다.
form.why: 낫다 is ㅅ-irregular: ㅅ drops before a vowel, so 낫 + 을 → 나을 거예요.

ko_meaning: 사람이 똑바로 섰을 때 발부터 머리까지의 길이
ko_meaning_en: The length from your feet to your head when you stand straight

example.en: Basketball players are really tall.

tokens.note: 들 = plural, 은 marks the topic

form.q_en: Pick the adjective Koreans use with 키 ('tall').
form.why: Height (키) goes with 크다/작다: 키가 커요 = is tall. 높다 is for buildings and mountains.

en: to be fat; to be chubby
ko_meaning_en: To have a lot of fat, so the body is wide

example.ko: 우리 개는 너무 많이 먹어서 뚱뚱해요.
example.roman: Uri gaeneun neomu mani meogeoseo ttungttunghaeyo.
example.en: Our dog eats too much, so it's fat.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 먹다 + -어서.
form.why: 먹 has ㅓ, so it takes -어서: 먹어서 (said [머거서]).

ko_meaning_en: To have a thin, nice-looking body

example.en: My older sister eats a lot, but she's slim.

form.q_en: Pick the connector meaning 'but'.
form.why: -지만 shows contrast: she eats a lot, but she's slim. -어서 and -(으)니까 mean 'because'.

en: to be good-looking; to be handsome
ko_meaning_en: To have a handsome, nice-looking face

example.en: That actor is really handsome.

tokens.note: looks are usually said with the past form

form.q_en: Koreans describe looks with the past form. Pick it.
form.why: 잘생기 + 었어요 → 잘생겼어요 (ㅣ + ㅓ → ㅕ). It means 'is good-looking' now.

ko_meaning_en: Small and pretty, so lovable

example.en: The little puppy is so cute.

form.q_en: Pick the correct present form of 귀엽다.
form.why: 귀엽다 is ㅂ-irregular: ㅂ becomes 우 before a vowel, so 귀엽 + 어요 → 귀여워요.

en: to be clear (sky); to be clean (water)
ko_meaning_en: To have no clouds and nice weather

example.ko: 오늘은 하늘이 맑아서 산이 잘 보여요.
example.roman: Oneureun haneuri malgaseo sani jal boyeoyo.
example.en: The sky is clear today, so I can see the mountains well.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 맑다 + -아서.
form.why: 맑 has ㅏ, so it takes -아서: 맑아서. It sounds like [말가서] but is spelled 맑아서.

ko_meaning_en: So many clouds that the sky is dark

example.en: Tomorrow it will be cloudy and rainy.

form.q_en: Pick the future form of 오다 ('will come').
form.why: After a vowel stem, add ㄹ: 오 + ㄹ → 올 거예요. 온 is a past modifier and does not fit 내일.

ko_meaning: 하늘에 떠 있는 하얗거나 회색인 것
ko_meaning_en: The white or gray things floating in the sky

example.en: There isn't a single cloud in the sky.

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject after a consonant
하나도 + negative = not a single one

form.q_en: Pick the phrase meaning 'not a single one' (with 없어요).
form.why: 하나도 + a negative means 'not even one'. 한 needs a counter, and 일 is not used this way.

ko_meaning_en: For the wind to move

example.en: It's very windy, so wear a hat.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 불다 + -(으)니까.
form.why: For a ㄹ-stem, ㄹ drops before ㄴ and no 으 is added: 불 + 니까 → 부니까.

ko_meaning: 비가 올 때 머리 위에 쓰는 물건
ko_meaning_en: Something you hold over your head when it rains

example.en: I left my umbrella on the subway when I got off.

tokens.note: 에 marks where something is put
을 marks the object after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 놓다 + -고.
form.why: -고 goes straight on the stem: 놓 + 고 → 놓고. It sounds like [노코] but is spelled 놓고.

ko_meaning_en: To have nothing dirty on it

example.en: The hotel room was spacious and clean, so it was nice.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 깨끗하다 + -아서/어서.
form.why: 하다 words take -여서, which becomes 해서: 깨끗해서.

ko_meaning_en: Not clean because dust or dirt is on it

example.en: Put dirty clothes in the washing machine.

tokens.note: ㅂ irregular modifier: 더럽 + 은 → 더러운

form.q_en: Pick the modifier form of 더럽다.
form.why: 더럽다 is ㅂ-irregular: ㅂ becomes 우 before -은, so 더럽 + 은 → 더러운.

ko_meaning_en: Having no sound, or only a little

example.en: I want to study at a quiet cafe.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the modifier form of 조용하다 ('quiet').
form.why: 조용하다 is an adjective, so the present modifier is -ㄴ: 조용한. -는 is only for verbs.

en: to be noisy; to be loud
ko_meaning_en: Sounds are too loud and too many

example.en: It's noisy outside, so please close the window.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 시끄럽다 + -(으)니까.
form.why: 시끄럽다 is ㅂ-irregular: ㅂ + 으 becomes 우, so 시끄럽 + 으니까 → 시끄러우니까.

en: to be comfortable; to be convenient
ko_meaning_en: Your body or mind feels at ease, not strained

example.en: These shoes are light and comfortable.

tokens.note: -고 = and; ㅂ stays before a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 가볍다 + -고 ('light and').
form.why: -고 goes straight on the stem: 가볍 + 고 → 가볍고. The ㅂ only changes before a vowel.

en: to be wide; to be spacious
ko_meaning_en: For a place such as a room or road to be big

example.en: This room is spacious and quiet.

form.q_en: Pick the right '-고' (and) form of 넓다.
form.why: -고 attaches straight to the stem 넓-, so it is 넓고. The ㄼ in the stem never drops in writing.

en: to be narrow; to be cramped
ko_meaning_en: For the space of a road or room to be small

example.ko: 이 길은 좁아서 차가 못 가요.
example.roman: I gireun jobaseo chaga mot gayo.
example.en: This road is narrow so cars can't get through.

form.q_en: Pick the form that gives the reason ('so').
form.why: 좁다 is regular (the ㅂ stays) and its stem has ㅗ, so it takes -아서: 좁아서.

ko_meaning_en: For the length to not be long

example.en: My younger sister likes short skirts.

tokens.note: -은 makes an adjective describe a noun

form.q_en: Pick the noun-modifier form of 짧다 ('short skirts').
form.why: Adjectives take -(으)ㄴ before a noun. 짧- ends in a consonant, so it is 짧은. -는 is for verbs.

ko_meaning_en: There is a lot of light so you can see well

example.en: The window is big so the room is bright.

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the right polite form of 밝다.
form.why: 밝다 has ㅏ in the stem, so it takes -아요: 밝아요 (said [발가요]).

ko_meaning_en: There is no light so you can't see well

example.en: The park is dark at night so it's scary.

form.q_en: Pick the right '-아서/어서' form of 어둡다.
form.why: 어둡다 is ㅂ-irregular: ㅂ becomes 우 before a vowel, so 어두 + 워서 → 어두워서.

ko_meaning_en: For two things to not be different from each other

example.en: My younger brother and I have the same birthday.

form.q_en: Pick the right polite form of 같다.
form.why: 같다 has ㅏ in the stem, so it takes -아요: 같아요 (said [가타요]).

ko_meaning_en: For things to not be the same as each other

example.en: These two bags are different colors.

tokens.note: 둘 becomes 두 before a noun

form.q_en: Pick the right polite form of 다르다.
form.why: 다르다 is 르-irregular: 르 drops, ㄹ is added and the stem vowel ㅏ brings -아요: 달라요.

ko_meaning: 답이 틀리지 않다; 옷이나 신발의 크기가 몸에 좋다
ko_meaning_en: An answer is not wrong; clothes or shoes are the right size

example.en: The teacher is right.

form.q_en: My answer is not right. Pick the form before 않아요.
form.why: -지 않다 makes a negative: the stem 맞- + 지 않아요 = 'is not right'.

ko_meaning_en: An answer or idea is not right

example.en: I got two questions wrong on the test.

form.q_en: Pick the right past form of 틀리다.
form.why: 틀리 + 었어요 contracts to 틀렸어요 (ㅣ + ㅓ → ㅕ).

ko_meaning_en: Something must be there

example.en: I need a big bag for the trip.

tokens.note: -ㄴ makes an adjective describe a noun
the needed thing is the subject

form.q_en: With 필요하다, which particle does the needed thing take?
form.why: 필요하다 is an adjective, so the needed thing is the subject. 가방 ends in a consonant, so 이 (not 가). 을 would be wrong.

ko_meaning_en: To be warm-hearted and nice to other people

example.en: The man at this store is really kind.

form.q_en: The man is kind, so I'll go again. Pick the reason form with -(으)니까.
form.why: -(으)니까 gives a reason. 친절하- ends in a vowel, so just add -니까: 친절하니까.

ko_meaning: 마음이 좋고 다른 사람을 잘 생각하다
ko_meaning_en: To have a good heart and care about others

example.en: My younger brother is good-natured and cute.

form.q_en: My brother is good-natured BUT noisy. Pick the 'but' form.
form.why: -지만 means 'but' and attaches straight to the stem: 착하 + 지만 → 착하지만.

ko_meaning_en: Many people know it well

example.en: This restaurant is famous for its bulgogi.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel

form.q_en: It's famous, so there are many people. Pick the reason form.
form.why: 하다 + 아서 becomes 해서: 유명해서 = 'because it is famous'.

ko_meaning_en: To not be old in age

example.en: Young people like this cafe.

form.q_en: Pick the noun-modifier form of 젊다.
form.why: 젊다 is an adjective ending in a consonant, so before a noun it takes -은: 젊은.

ko_meaning_en: To become older in age

example.en: Grandpa's dog has gotten very old.

tokens.note: 늙다 is a verb, so 'is old' uses the past

form.q_en: 늙다 is a verb, so 'has grown old' uses the past tense. Pick it.
form.why: 늙다 has ㅡ in the stem, so it takes -었어요: 늙었어요 (said [늘거써요]).

ko_meaning_en: To bring something new into being

example.en: I made rice cakes with Mom on the weekend.

form.q_en: Pick the right future form of 만들다.
form.why: 만들- already ends in ㄹ, so -(으)ㄹ 거예요 adds nothing more: 만들 거예요.

ko_meaning: 필요한 것이 어디에 있는지 알려고 하다
ko_meaning_en: To try to learn where something you need is

example.en: I found a Korean book at the library.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the form that means 'go (in order) to look for'.
form.why: -(으)러 shows purpose before 가다/오다. 찾- ends in a consonant, so it takes -으러: 찾으러.

ko_meaning_en: Something you had goes missing

example.en: I lost my umbrella on the subway.

form.q_en: I lost my umbrella, so I bought a new one. Pick the reason form.
form.why: 버리 + 어서 contracts to 버려서. Don't add the past tense before -아서/어서.

ko_meaning: 물건이나 편지를 다른 곳으로 가게 하다
ko_meaning_en: To make a thing or letter go somewhere else

example.en: I sent a letter at the post office.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the right past form of 보내다.
form.why: 보내 + 었어요 contracts to 보냈어요.

ko_meaning_en: To take what someone gives you

example.en: I got a lot of flowers on my birthday.

form.q_en: Can I get a receipt? Pick the form before 수 있어요.
form.why: -(으)ㄹ 수 있다 = can. 받- ends in a consonant, so it is 받을 수 있어요.

ko_meaning: 모르는 것을 알 수 있게 알려 주다
ko_meaning_en: To show someone what they don't know so they can learn it

example.en: I teach English at a school.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the right future form: 'Next year I will teach Korean.'
form.why: 가르치- ends in a vowel, so -(으)ㄹ 거예요 adds just ㄹ: 가르칠 거예요.

ko_meaning_en: To use your head to try to understand something

example.en: When I think of my family at night I feel sad.

form.q_en: Pick the ending that means 'when/if'.
form.why: -(으)면 = if/when. 생각하- ends in a vowel, so just add -면: 생각하면.

ko_meaning_en: To do something many times to get good at it

example.en: My younger brother practices taekwondo every day.

form.q_en: I have a test, so I have to practice every day. Pick the 'have to' form.
form.why: -아야/어야 하다 = have to. For 하다 verbs it becomes 해야: 연습해야 해요.

ko_meaning: 어떤 일을 하기 전에 필요한 것을 먼저 하다
ko_meaning_en: To do the needed things before something happens

example.en: Guests were coming in the evening so I prepared food.

form.q_en: Pick the right past form of 준비하다.
form.why: For 하다 verbs, the past polite form is 했어요: 준비했어요.

ko_meaning: 어떤 일이 다 되어서 더 하지 않다
ko_meaning_en: Something is all done and doesn't go on any more

example.en: What time does the class end?

form.q_en: 끝나다 does not take an object. Pick the particle.
form.why: With 끝나다 the class is the subject: 수업 ends in a consonant, so 이. 을 would need the verb 끝내다.

ko_meaning_en: To be on your feet, not sitting or lying

example.en: There were no seats on the bus so I stood the whole way.

form.q_en: Pick the polite request: 'Please stand here.'
form.why: -(으)세요 after a vowel stem: 서 + 세요 → 서세요.

ko_meaning_en: To lay your body down flat on the floor or a bed

example.en: I had a headache so I lay down on the bed.

form.q_en: Pick the right past form of 눕다.
form.why: 눕다 is ㅂ-irregular: ㅂ becomes 우, so 누 + 웠어요 → 누웠어요.

ko_meaning_en: To move your feet quickly to go forward

example.en: The children are running in the park.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: My leg hurts, so I can't run. Pick the form before 수 없어요.
form.why: -(으)ㄹ 수 없다 = can't. 뛰- ends in a vowel, so add ㄹ: 뛸 수 없어요.

ko_meaning_en: To go from below to above

example.en: I went up a mountain with a friend on the weekend.

form.q_en: Pick the right future form of 올라가다.
form.why: 올라가- ends in a vowel, so -(으)ㄹ 거예요 adds just ㄹ: 올라갈 거예요.

ko_meaning_en: To go from above to below

example.en: I went down to the kitchen to drink some water.

form.q_en: I went down to the first floor and then bought coffee. Pick the 'and then' form.
form.why: 가 + 아서 → 가서, so 내려가서 = 'went down and (then)'.

ko_meaning_en: To have something in your hand or raise it up

example.ko: 가방이 무거워서 혼자 들 수 없어요.
example.roman: Gabangi mugeowoseo honja deul su eopseoyo.
example.en: The bag is heavy so I can't lift it alone.

form.q_en: Pick the right form before 수 있어요: 'Can you hold this bag?'
form.why: 들- already ends in ㄹ, so -(으)ㄹ 수 있다 adds nothing: 들 수 있어요.

ko_meaning_en: To leave a thing in some place

example.en: I put the cup on the desk.

tokens.note: ㅗ in the stem → -았어요; ㅎ is silent

form.q_en: Pick the right polite request: 'Please put your bag here.'
form.why: 놓- ends in a consonant, so it takes -으세요: 놓으세요.

ko_meaning_en: To take hold of something with your hand and not let go

example.en: The child held Mom's hand.

form.q_en: Pick the right past form of 잡다.
form.why: 잡다 is NOT ㅂ-irregular (unlike 덥다); it keeps ㅂ and takes -았어요: 잡았어요.

ko_meaning: 다른 사람의 것을 얼마 동안 쓰려고 받다
ko_meaning_en: To take someone else's thing to use for a while

example.en: I borrowed a little money from a friend.

form.q_en: I borrowed a book and then read it at home. Pick the 'and then' form.
form.why: 빌리 + 어서 → 빌려서. Here -아서/어서 means 'and then (with it)'.

ko_meaning_en: To give back something you borrowed

example.en: I'm going to give the book back to my friend tomorrow.

form.q_en: You have to give back a borrowed book. Pick the 'have to' form.
form.why: 주 + 어야 → 줘야, so 돌려줘야 해요 = 'have to give back'.

ko_meaning_en: A letter sent and received over the internet

example.en: I get a lot of emails every day at work.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the object particle for 이메일.
form.why: 이메일 ends in ㄹ (a consonant), so the object particle is 을, not 를.

ko_meaning_en: A short piece of writing sent by cell phone

example.en: Send me a text when you get home.

form.q_en: Pick the object particle for 문자.
form.why: 문자 ends in a vowel, so the object particle is 를.

ko_meaning: 종이에 써서 다른 사람에게 보내는 글
ko_meaning_en: Writing on paper that you send to someone

example.en: I read the letter my grandmother wrote.

form.q_en: Pick the right modifier: 'the letter (that) Grandma wrote'.
form.why: 쓰- ends in a vowel, so the past noun modifier is -ㄴ: 쓴 편지 = the letter someone wrote.

ko_meaning: 전화나 문자로 다른 사람에게 소식을 알리다
ko_meaning_en: To give someone news by phone or text

example.en: Get in touch if you have time.

form.q_en: Pick the polite 'I will' form with -겠어요.
form.why: -겠어요 attaches to the stem: 연락하 + 겠어요 → 연락하겠어요 ('I will contact you').

ko_meaning_en: To make a phone call and talk

example.en: I called my parents yesterday.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for the person you call.
form.why: Use 에게 for the person you call ('to'). 에서 is for places, and 전화하다 does not take a person as an object with 을.

ko_meaning_en: A phone you carry around and use

example.en: I left my cell phone at home.

form.q_en: Pick the subject particle for 핸드폰.
form.why: 핸드폰 ends in a consonant (ㄴ), so the subject particle is 이.

ko_meaning: 컴퓨터나 핸드폰으로 여러 가지를 찾고 볼 수 있는 것
ko_meaning_en: What lets you find and see many things on a computer or phone

example.en: I found a cheap plane ticket on the internet.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the particle for where you do something online.
form.why: 에서 marks the place where an action happens: 인터넷에서 = on the internet.

ko_meaning_en: Numbers given to something to show which it is

example.en: Write your name and number on your bag.

form.q_en: Pick 'and' after 번호.
form.why: 번호 ends in a vowel, so 'and' is 와. 과 is used after a consonant.

ko_meaning: 사는 곳이나 건물이 있는 곳을 나타낸 것
ko_meaning_en: What shows where someone lives or where a building is

example.en: What is my friend's home address?

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the subject particle for 주소.
form.why: 주소 ends in a vowel, so the subject particle is 가.

ko_meaning: 다른 사람이 모르게 나만 아는 번호
ko_meaning_en: A number only you know, so others can't use it

example.ko: 비밀번호를 몰라서 문을 열 수 없어요.
example.roman: Bimilbeonhoreul mollaseo muneul yeol su eopseoyo.
example.en: I don't know the password so I can't open the door.

form.q_en: Pick the object particle for 비밀번호.
form.ko: 비밀번호___ 몰라서 문을 열 수 없어요.
form.why: 비밀번호 is the object of 모르다 and ends in a vowel, so it takes 를.

ko_meaning_en: Not often, just once in a while

example.en: On weekends I sometimes watch movies alone.

form.q_en: Pick the adverb that fits this positive sentence.
form.why: 가끔 works in a positive sentence. 전혀 and 별로 need a negative, and 아까 (a while ago) needs the past tense.

ko_meaning: 특별한 일이 없을 때 거의 언제나
ko_meaning_en: Almost always, when nothing special is happening

example.en: I usually get up at seven.

form.q_en: I usually don't eat breakfast. Pick the form before 않아요.
form.why: -지 않다 makes a negative: the stem 먹- + 지 않아요.

ko_meaning_en: Not even a little (followed by 안, 못 or 없다)

example.ko: 저는 매운 음식을 전혀 못 먹어요.
example.roman: Jeoneun maeun eumsigeul jeonhyeo mot meogeoyo.
example.en: I can't eat spicy food at all.

form.q_en: 전혀 needs a negative. Pick the right ending.
form.why: 전혀 is used only with negative words like 안, 못 or 없다.

ko_meaning_en: Not that much (followed by 안 or -지 않다)

example.en: It's not that cold today.

form.q_en: This stew is not very spicy. Pick the form before 않아요.
form.why: -지 않다 follows the stem: 맵 + 지 않아요. 별로 goes with negative forms like this.

ko_meaning_en: Not all, but close to all

example.en: I've almost finished my homework.

form.q_en: Pick the word for 'almost': 'Almost all my friends came.'
form.why: 거의 다 = almost all. 전혀 and 별로 need a negative, and 내일 (tomorrow) does not fit the past tense.

ko_meaning_en: Much more than you expected

example.en: These pants are too long.

form.q_en: It was too spicy, so I couldn't eat it. Pick the reason form.
form.why: 맵다 is ㅂ-irregular: 매 + 워서 → 매워서.

ko_meaning_en: Truly, not a lie

example.en: Korean winters are really cold.

form.q_en: This kimchi is really spicy BUT tasty. Pick the 'but' form.
form.why: -지만 attaches straight to the stem: 맵 + 지만 → 맵지만. ㅂ does not change before a consonant.

ko_meaning_en: First among many

example.ko: 저는 과일 중에서 딸기를 제일 좋아해요.
example.roman: Jeoneun gwail jung-eseo ttalgireul jeil joahaeyo.
example.en: Of all fruits I like strawberries the most.

form.q_en: Pick the word: 'Of all seasons I like summer the most.'
form.why: 제일 = the most. 전혀 and 별로 need a negative, and 방금 (just now) does not fit.

ko_meaning_en: More than something else

example.en: I want to eat more rice.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for 'than': 'The train is faster than the bus.'
form.why: N보다 더 = more than N, so 버스보다 더 빨라요 = faster than the bus.

ko_meaning_en: Without forgetting, whatever happens

example.en: Tomorrow I'll be sure to come early.

form.q_en: You must do your homework. Pick the 'have to' form.
form.why: 하다 + -아야/어야 → 해야, so 꼭 해야 해요 = must do.

ko_meaning_en: Just yourself, without anyone else

example.en: My older brother lives alone in Seoul.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: I plan to live alone next year. Pick the 'plan to' form.
form.why: 살- ends in ㄹ, so -(으)려고 adds just 려고: 살려고 해요 = plan to live.

ko_meaning_en: All, with nothing left out

example.en: Everyone in my family is tall.

form.q_en: Pick the right present form of 크다.
form.why: In 크다, ㅡ drops before -어요: 크 + 어요 → 커요.

ko_meaning_en: Everything, with nothing left

example.en: I was hungry so I ate all the rice.

form.q_en: Pick the reason form of 고프다.
form.why: In 고프다, ㅡ drops, and the vowel before it (ㅗ) brings -아서: 고파서.

ko_meaning_en: Very nicely; without mistakes

example.en: My older sister sings really well.

form.q_en: Pick the word that means 'well' (not the adjective 좋다).
form.why: 잘 is the adverb 'well' and can go before a verb. 좋은, 좋아요 and 좋다 are forms of the adjective 좋다.

ko_meaning: 어떤 일을 할 수 없다는 뜻의 말
ko_meaning_en: A word meaning you are unable to do something

example.en: I hurt my leg so I can't play soccer.

tokens.note: 못 goes right before the verb

form.q_en: 못 가요 means the same as ___ 수 없어요. Pick the form.
form.why: 못 가요 = 갈 수 없어요 (cannot go). -(으)ㄹ 수 없다 needs the -(으)ㄹ form: 갈.

ko_meaning: 앞의 말과 뒤의 말을 이어 주는 말
ko_meaning_en: A word that joins what comes before and after

example.en: And I bought eggs too.

form.q_en: Pick the word for 'and' that adds another fact.
form.why: 그리고 adds another fact. 하지만 shows contrast, 그러면 a condition and 그래서 a result, which don't fit.

ko_meaning: 이야기를 바꾸거나 앞과 다른 말을 할 때 쓰는 말
ko_meaning_en: Used to change the topic or say something different

example.en: By the way, what's your name?

form.q_en: Pick the word that changes the topic ('by the way').
form.why: 그런데 turns to a new topic. 그래서/그러니까 give a result and 그래도 means 'even so', which don't fit.

ko_meaning: 앞의 일 때문에 뒤의 일이 생길 때 쓰는 말
ko_meaning_en: Used when the earlier thing causes the later thing

example.en: So I couldn't go to school today.

form.q_en: Pick the word that shows a result.
form.why: 그래서 = so (result). 그래도 and 하지만 show contrast, and 그런데 changes the topic.

ko_meaning: 앞의 말과 반대되는 말을 할 때 쓰는 말
ko_meaning_en: Used to say the opposite of what came before

example.en: But the price is too high.

form.q_en: Pick the word that shows contrast.
form.why: 하지만 = but/however. 그래서 and 그러니까 give a result, and 그러면 a condition.

ko_meaning: 앞의 말이 맞으면 또는 그렇게 하면
ko_meaning_en: If what was said is so, or if you do that

example.en: Then please come again tomorrow.

form.q_en: Pick the word meaning 'in that case'.
form.why: 그러면 = then, in that case. 그래도 and 하지만 show contrast, and 그리고 just adds.

ko_meaning: 앞의 일이 있어도 뒤의 일이 바뀌지 않을 때 쓰는 말
ko_meaning_en: Used when the later thing stays the same despite the earlier thing

example.en: Even so I exercise every day.

form.q_en: Pick the word meaning 'even so'.
form.ko: 비가 많이 와요. ___ 산에 갈 거예요.
form.why: 그래도 = even so. 그래서, 그러니까 and 그러면 would make going up the mountain a result of the rain.

ko_meaning: 앞의 말이 뒤의 말의 이유일 때 쓰는 말
ko_meaning_en: Used when the earlier words are the reason for the later ones

example.en: So be sure to take an umbrella.

form.q_en: Before a request, which 'so' is natural?
form.why: 그래서 cannot come before a request or suggestion; use 그러니까. 하지만 and 그래도 show contrast.

ko_meaning: 한 번 더; 그 위에 더
ko_meaning_en: One more time; on top of that

example.ko: 어제 간 식당에 또 가고 싶어요.
example.roman: Eoje gan sikdang-e tto gago sipeoyo.
example.en: I want to go again to the restaurant I went to yesterday.

form.q_en: Pick the past noun modifier: 'the restaurant I went to yesterday'.
form.why: A past action before a noun takes -(으)ㄴ: 어제 간 식당. -는 is present and -(으)ㄹ is future.

ko_meaning: 꼭은 아니지만 그럴 것 같을 때 쓰는 말
ko_meaning_en: Used when something is likely but not certain

example.en: It will probably rain tomorrow.

form.q_en: 아마 goes with a guess about the future. Pick the ending.
form.why: 아마 usually comes with -(으)ㄹ 거예요 to make a guess: 올 거예요.

ko_meaning_en: Very fast, in a way you didn't expect

example.ko: 갑자기 비가 와서 옷이 다 젖었어요.
example.roman: Gapjagi biga waseo osi da jeojeosseoyo.
example.en: It suddenly rained so my clothes got all wet.

form.q_en: It suddenly rained, so I bought an umbrella. Pick the reason form.
form.why: 오 + 아서 → 와서. Don't put the past tense before -아서/어서.

ko_meaning_en: A very short time ago

example.en: My friend just got home.

form.q_en: 방금 talks about the past. Pick the ending.
form.why: 방금 means 'just now', so the verb must be past: 출발했어요.

ko_meaning_en: A little while ago

example.en: The rice cake I ate earlier was really delicious.

form.q_en: Pick the past noun modifier: 'the rice cake I ate earlier'.
form.why: A past action before a noun takes -(으)ㄴ. 먹- ends in a consonant, so 먹은.

ko_meaning_en: After a little time passes

example.en: Let's have lunch together in a bit.

form.q_en: 이따가 is about later. Pick the ending.
form.why: 이따가 points to the near future, so use -(으)ㄹ 거예요: 전화할 거예요.

ko_meaning_en: Without stopping

example.en: The baby keeps crying at night.

form.q_en: The baby kept crying, so I couldn't sleep. Pick the reason form.
form.why: 울다 has ㅜ, so it takes -어서: 울어서. Don't add the past tense before -어서.

ko_meaning_en: In a very short time

example.en: If you take this medicine you'll get better soon.

form.q_en: Pick the right polite form of 낫다.
